ArtemisFingerprintRequest.description:
A single HTTP response submitted for offline technology fingerprinting.

The caller supplies a response they already captured (status, headers and an
optional body). No request is ever sent from the server: fingerprinting is a
pure match against the curated signature set.
ArtemisFingerprintRequest.title: ArtemisFingerprintRequest

ArtemisFingerprintResult.description: Versioned Artemis passive-fingerprint result shared by API and Web.
ArtemisFingerprintResult.title: ArtemisFingerprintResult

ArtemisFingerprintView.description: One matched technology projected for API clients and the Web UI.
ArtemisFingerprintView.title: ArtemisFingerprintView

AthenaPlanRequest.description:
Engagement inputs that turn a named profile into a validated plan.

No target is ever assumed and ``confirmed`` must be set explicitly: a profile
never self-authorizes a run, so an unconfirmed request fails validation (422)
rather than yielding a silently runnable plan. Building a plan is a pure,
offline, network-free computation — it produces a signable document, it does
not execute anything.
AthenaPlanRequest.title: AthenaPlanRequest

AthenaPlanView.description: Versioned, bounded projection of a built Athena plan for API and Web.
AthenaPlanView.title: AthenaPlanView

AthenaProfileList.description: Versioned list of the named scan profiles Athena can build plans from.
AthenaProfileList.title: AthenaProfileList

AthenaProfileView.description: A target-free scan profile projected for API clients and the Web UI.
AthenaProfileView.title: AthenaProfileView

AttackAssociationView.description: One suggested CWE→ATT&CK association attached to a finding explanation.
AttackAssociationView.title: AttackAssociationView

Confidence.description: How confident Olympus is that a finding is a true positive.
Confidence.title: Confidence

CorrelationModel.description: The versioned, published shape of one correlation (``CORR-1``).
CorrelationModel.title: CorrelationModel

CorrelationsDocument.description: The versioned, published shape of a set of correlations (``CORR-1``).
CorrelationsDocument.title: CorrelationsDocument

DetectionRule.description: A minimal portable detection rule expressed as YAML-compatible JSON.
DetectionRule.title: DetectionRule

Engagement.description:
The top-level container that groups an authorized assessment's work.

An engagement owns its scope and authorization reference; assets, scans,
jobs, findings, evidence, alerts, incidents and reports are associated with
it by ``engagement_id``. CLI, TUI, API and Web all reference this one model
(ROADMAP ``WEB-B``) rather than a private per-interface notion of scope.
Engagement.title: Engagement

EngagementList.description: The engagements visible over the API, newest first.
EngagementList.title: EngagementList

EngagementManifest.description: Immutable authorization boundary for one time-limited engagement.
EngagementManifest.title: EngagementManifest

EngagementScope.description:
The authorized perimeter of an engagement: included minus excluded.

Entries are hostnames or domains (matched like the rest of Olympus: an entry
covers itself and its subdomains). IP/CIDR matching is a planned extension
(ROADMAP ``WEB-B``); until then IPs must be listed verbatim.
EngagementScope.title: EngagementScope

EngagementStatus.description: Lifecycle state of an engagement (the top-level assessment container).
EngagementStatus.title: EngagementStatus

EpistemicClass.description:
What kind of knowledge a statement is (ROADMAP ``EXPL-1``/``CORR-1``).

Shared across explainability (`EXPL-1`) and correlation (`CORR-1`) so every
surface labels a claim by how it is known. The ordering is from strongest to
weakest epistemic standing; a weaker class must never be presented as a
stronger one (an inference is not an observation, a hypothesis is not a
demonstrated compromise).
EpistemicClass.title: EpistemicClass

EpistemicStatementView.description: One explanation claim with the epistemic class saying how it is known.
EpistemicStatementView.title: EpistemicStatementView

Lifecycle state of one durable job.

The terminal states are deliberately distinct: collapsing them into
``failed`` hides whether a scan broke, was refused, ran out of time, or
never ran at all.

MinervaLedgerEntryView.description: Normalized, bounded projection of one verified custody entry.
MinervaLedgerEntryView.title: MinervaLedgerEntryView

MinervaLedgerVerification.description:
Versioned Minerva custody verification result for API and Web clients.

The hash chain is always verified (a non-error result means it held). The
signature is verified only when the server is configured with the matching
Ed25519 verification key and the ledger is signed; otherwise a signed ledger
reports ``signature_verified=false`` so the caller refuses to trust it.
MinervaLedgerVerification.title: MinervaLedgerVerification

MinervaLedgerVerificationRequest.description:
A custody ledger document submitted for offline integrity verification.

The ledger is the exact JSON object produced by Minerva custody
(``olympus.custody``). It is verified in memory: no filesystem path, no key
and no evidence payload is ever accepted from the caller.

ledger.description: The olympus.custody ledger document to verify, as a JSON object.
ledger.title: Ledger

MinervaLedgerVerificationRequest.title: MinervaLedgerVerificationRequest

ProteusCampaignValidationRequest.description: Non-target awareness-campaign metadata submitted for offline validation.
ProteusCampaignValidationRequest.title: ProteusCampaignValidationRequest

ProteusCampaignValidationResult.description: Versioned, normalized campaign metadata (no email is ever sent).
ProteusCampaignValidationResult.title: ProteusCampaignValidationResult

RiskClass.description:
How intrusive one scanner is against a target, worst-case.

The ordering is meaningful: ``PASSIVE < ACTIVE < INTRUSIVE <
DESTRUCTIVE_PROHIBITED``. The first three drive how much friction the guided
flow puts in front of a launch. ``DESTRUCTIVE_PROHIBITED`` is different in
kind: it is a **declared product boundary**, not a launchable class — no
catalogued scanner carries it, and :func:`within_product_scope` is ``False``
for it, so a capability classified this way is refused, never run.
RiskClass.title: RiskClass

RiskFactorView.description: One contribution to the contextual risk score, in plain language.
RiskFactorView.title: RiskFactorView

Severity.description: Normalized severity scale shared by findings, alerts and reports.
Severity.title: Severity

SignedEngagementManifest.description: A manifest plus its detached Ed25519 signature and pinned digest.
SignedEngagementManifest.title: SignedEngagementManifest

Source.description: Producing module for a given object (provenance).
Source.title: Source

ThemisJob.description:
Versioned job document returned consistently by CLI, API and workers.

``3.0.0`` adds the digest of the signed engagement manifest. Legacy jobs
migrate with ``None`` rather than receiving invented authorization provenance.
ThemisJob.title: ThemisJob

VulcanCorrelateRequest.description:
Bounded inputs for offline correlation (``CORR-2`` API surface).

Correlates a set of findings (``asset-overlap`` / ``shared-cve`` /
``shared-evidence``) and, when both ``indicators`` and ``events`` are given,
the cross-module ``ioc-event`` leads. At least ``findings``, or both
``indicators`` and ``events`` together, must be supplied — the same rule the
CLI enforces, so an empty request cannot masquerade as a zero-result answer.
VulcanCorrelateRequest.title: VulcanCorrelateRequest

VulcanFindingExplanationResult.description:
Versioned finding explanation (``EXPL-1``) shared by CLI, API and reports.

The API projects the exact :class:`~olympus.vulcan.explain.FindingExplanation`
contract, so every surface answers *why this finding, why this risk, how sure*
identically (`EXPL-2` parity).
VulcanFindingExplanationResult.title: VulcanFindingExplanationResult

info.description: Authorized specialist-engine orchestration and evidence lifecycle.
info.title: Olympus Themis API

post.description:
Extract in-domain subdomains from a Certificate Transparency export, offline.

The caller supplies the exact crt.sh JSON array (`?output=json`); it is
parsed locally with the same core as `olympus argus ct`. No Certificate
Transparency query is issued from the server. Only names that are a
subdomain of the given domain and are conservative ASCII DNS hostnames are
returned, deduplicated and sorted; a wildcard prefix is normalized away.

Fingerprint a captured HTTP response against the curated signatures, offline.

The caller supplies a response they already captured (status, headers and
an optional body); it is matched locally with the same core as the Artemis
scanner. No request is ever sent from the server — this is a passive match,
never an active probe.

Build a validated, signable assessment plan from a named profile, offline.

The profile supplies adapters and safe limits; the caller supplies the
authorized target(s), engagement scope and authorization reference.
Building a plan is a pure, deterministic computation: it produces a plan
document, it never executes a scan. ``confirmed`` must be true — a profile
never self-authorizes a run — so an unconfirmed or out-of-shape request is
rejected with 422 rather than yielding a silently runnable plan.

get.description:
List the named, target-free scan profiles Athena can build plans from.

A profile only chooses which already-registered adapters run and with
which safe limits; it carries no target and performs no network access.

schema.title: Response Capabilities Api V1 Capabilities Get

post.description:
Identify a service passively from a captured banner and/or port, offline.

The caller supplies what they already observed; no probe is ever sent from
the server. A volunteered banner is the only evidence: it is sanitised and
matched locally. A port number is a convention, not proof — it is used only
as a fallback and the result says so (``identified_from``). An unknown
banner is reported honestly, never upgraded into a claim.

Scan submitted text for secrets offline, returning only masked findings.

The caller submits text (never a path to walk); detection is local and
deterministic, using the same core as the Hermes scanner. Every finding's
value is **masked** before it leaves the server — a raw secret is never
echoed back — and each carries a stable fingerprint for de-duplication.

Extract IOCs from free text, a STIX bundle or a MISP event, offline.

Parsing and normalization are local and deterministic; no network access,
collection or enrichment is performed. Unparsed or unmapped input is
returned in ``skipped`` with a reason, never silently dropped.

Validate and normalize awareness-campaign metadata, offline.

Checks the non-target campaign fields with the same core as the Proteus
campaign builder (header hygiene, a normalized sender address and a bounded
landing URL) **before** any authorization or scope access. No email is ever
sent and no target is contacted; invalid input is a 422 with the reason.

Correlate findings — and optionally Metis IOCs against Apollo events — offline.

Projects the same versioned ``olympus.correlations`` document the CLI
renders, from the single shared ``vulcan.correlate.correlations_document``
core: deterministic identity joins (``asset-overlap`` / ``shared-cve`` /
``shared-evidence``) plus, when indicators and events are supplied, the
``ioc-event`` threat-intel leads (``suggested_correlation`` — never
presented as a fact or a compromise). Pure and offline: no scan, no
network request is ever made from the server.

Explain one finding with the shared ``EXPL-1`` contract, offline.

The caller supplies a ``olympus.finding`` and receives the same
:class:`~olympus.vulcan.explain.FindingExplanation` the CLI and the reports
render — derived only from the finding's own fields, nothing fetched or
invented, with every claim tagged by its epistemic class. Pure and offline:
no scanning and no network request is ever made from the server.
